Subject: Re: Galaxy-7B: brief update on elevated errors (NimbleHealth) — technical findings

Quick technical notes / root-cause hypothesis:
- Observed a correlated uptick in long-context batch requests from a small set of customers at ~22:00 UTC which increased KV-cache churn.
- Metric spike: avg KV cache eviction rate +410% vs baseline; memory pressure triggered more frequent kernel fallbacks on select runners.
- On affected hosts the model runtime hit a path that produced blocking retries (leading to 503s/timeouts) under heavy concurrent long sequences.

Mitigation performed by 23:30 UTC:
- Rolled a targeted kernel rollback on the affected runner image (rollback documented in runbook_rollback_steps.pdf).
- Scaled the Galaxy-7B pool + prefetched larger KV cache allocation for long-sequence workloads.
- Enabled a temporary per-account long-context throttling rule for NimbleHealth to limit concurrent very-long requests (we informed them via Priyom).

Result: by 23:40 UTC error rate for Galaxy-7B requests dropped to baseline (~<1%). We continued to monitor for recurrence overnight. Attached: galaxy7b_kv_eviction_snapshot.json (snapshot) and runbook_rollback_steps.pdf.

Next steps for full postmortem: Marcus / Product to validate kernel change and propose permanent mitigations (KV sizing heuristics + improved detection). I’ll capture the incident in RW-9583.

— Soojin

Subject: Galaxy-7B incident summary, impact mitigations, and next steps (RW-9583)

Hi Olivia / Arturo — following up with a short incident summary and next steps. Thank you for your patience overnight.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-06-17 22:05–23:40 UTC (elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting Galaxy-7B).
- Impact: transient failures for ~10–15% of Galaxy-7B generation requests for select customers (NimbleHealth saw batch job retries). No data loss; requests either retried or routed to fallback.
- Root cause (preliminary): KV-cache eviction surge and memory pressure on select runners triggered a kernel fallback path that produced blocking retries under heavy long-context concurrency.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: fallback routing to Galaxy-7B-quant, autoscale bump, kernel rollback on affected hosts, KV sizing prefetch, temporary per-account throttling.
- Ongoing: RW-9583 ticket created; Marcus will own permanent mitigations including KV heuristics, better long-context detection, and an automated fallback earlier in the runtime.

Compensation & follow-up:
- We’ve opened a request with billing for a one-time usage credit to offset retry costs; I’ll share details once processed.
- Postmortem doc + timeline will be shared by Tue 2026-06-22.
- Propose a short 30-min technical walkthrough with your engineering team and our SREs on Thu 2026-06-20 to review mitigations and recommended configuration changes. Please let me know if that works.

Attachments: nimble_support_log_06-17.txt (log snippet), runbook_rollback_steps.pdf.

If you want earlier access to the raw logs or a scoped support re-run of affected jobs, we can schedule it — tell me which job IDs and we’ll prioritize.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’re treating this as high priority and will follow through on action items.

Best,
